description: fEGarch OUTPUT fixtures for the quantica clean-room port (Phase 0). Generated by running fEGarch's PUBLIC functions and recording numeric output; no fEGarch source was read (CLAUDE.md §12). R is never a quantica/CI dependency.

distribution_fixtures.method: fEGarch exposes standardized SAMPLERS (r*_s) but no public density/CDF/quantile functions, so distributions are characterised by sampler output: empirical moments and quantiles. Python compares its analytic values within Monte-Carlo tolerance.
distribution_fixtures.reconcile: ALD uses fEGarch's `P` parameter (default 8) — the exact average-Laplace form is a RECONCILE item; the skew variants use fEGarch's `skew` (1 = symmetric). These fixtures are what lock the ALD form and the Fernandez-Steel normalization on the Python side.

diag_garch11_norm.note: Phase-6 diagnostics (residual fit-tests): the FULL-sample GARCH(1,1)/norm fit (fit_params == fit_garch11_norm) run through fit_test_suite. All three operate on the FITTED MODEL object (S4 method for signature 'fEGarch_fit'), computing standardized residuals internally as etat = (rt - cmeans)/sigt. (1) ljung_box_test -- WEIGHTED Ljung-Box (Fisher-Gallagher 2012 linearly-decreasing weights (m_max+1-lag)/m_max, Gamma-approx null), applied to the SIMPLE (level) and SQUARED (volatility) standardized residuals for lags m=1..m_max (default 20); adj_df: simple = sum of ARMA params (0 here, constant mean), squared = 0. (2) sign_bias_test -- Engle-Ng (1993) regression of squared std residuals on lagged sign/size dummies; four rows (Sign bias, Negative sign bias, Positive sign bias, Joint). (3) goodn_of_fit_test -- adjusted Pearson chi-square on the PIT u = F_eta(etat) binned into equal-probability bins at n_bins in {20,30,40,50}, df = n_bins-1. CONVENTION FINDING: every test returns ONLY p-values (LB: m+pval; sign-bias: pval; GoF: n_bins+df+pval) -- the raw statistics are NOT exposed in the returned matrices. To validate the clean-room build, reproduce these p-values (and df) from the standardized residuals.

predict_garch11_norm.note: Phase-6 multi-step predict (n.ahead point forecast; DISTINCT from predict_roll's one-step rolling). GARCH(1,1)/norm TRAINING fit (n_test=250, same fit as forecast_garch11_norm/predict_roll); predict(n.ahead=10 & 50) -> sigt/cmeans over the horizon (CSV cols h,sigma,cmeans). REVIEW FINDING: multi-step is the standard NAIVE ITERATED variance forecast -- sigma^2_{n+h} = omega + (phi1+beta1)*sigma^2_{n+h-1} for h>=2 (1-step = omega+phi1*eps_n^2+beta1*sigma^2_n) -- reproduced from the training-end state to 1.7e-18 (h10) / 6.9e-18 (h50), MACHINE-EXACT. Converges to the unconditional variance omega/(1-phi1-beta1)=1.531e-4 (sigma_inf=0.012373); at h=50 sigma=0.011873 (still climbing, phi1+beta1=0.977 -> slow). No bias issue: GARCH variance forecast is linear/unbiased. cmeans constant = mu. predict h=1 sigma == forecast_roll_sigma[0] exactly (1-step == first rolling forecast).

predict_egarch11_norm.note: Phase-6 multi-step predict for the Type-I EGF (EGARCH(1,1)/norm, FULL-sample fit == fit_egarch11_norm). REVIEW FINDING (the paper-flagged E[exp(g(eta))] bias case): predict is the NAIVE/BIASED iterated forecast -- iterate ln sigma^2 forward with the future news term g(eta)=0 by construction (ln sigma^2_{n+h} = omega + phi1*ln sigma^2_{n+h-1}, h>=2; 1-step uses the known eta_n), then report sigma = exp(ln sigma^2 / 2). NO bias correction is applied: reproduced this naive form to 1.7e-17 (h10) / 1.9e-17 (h50), MACHINE-EXACT. Consequence: sigma converges to exp(E[ln sigma^2]/2) = exp(omega_sig/2) = 0.011349, NOT E[sigma] (the Jensen/E[exp(g/2)] term is left in). This is what makes EGF multi-step 'biased' -- fEGarch's predict does the naive iterate, exactly reproducible. cmeans constant = mu.

_forecast_breadth: Phase-6 forecasting BREADTH (branch feat/fegarch-forecast-breadth): the forecast engine (predict_roll, predict) is UNCHANGED; these fixtures extend the distribution axis of the two models it reproduces -- GARCH (rolling + multi-step) and EGARCH (multi-step). The sigma-hat recursion is distribution-independent, so each law reproduces the norm mechanism to machine precision; the DISTRIBUTION bites in the GARCH rolling VaR/ES (measure_risk uses the fitted law) and the EGARCH h=1 news g(eta_n) (E|eta| centering). EGARCH covers 5 non-norm (ged/ald/snorm/sged/sald), NOT 7: fEGarch errors on egarch x std/sstd (continuous-df Type-I EGF, spec-notes 20) -> no output to reproduce. EGARCH rolling is not generated (predict_roll is GARCH-only).

_forecast_fi_family: Forecast family 2 (branch feat/fegarch-forecast-fi): the FI long-memory multi-step + rolling forecasts -- FIGARCH/FIEGARCH/FIGJR/FITGARCH/FIAPARCH, the fractional versions of the bases on main. NEW forecast math (spec-notes §34), gated before engine code. The (1-L)^d weights are EXTENDED by the horizon and the forecast conditions on the observed sample with PRE-SAMPLE 0 (the in-sample Var/mean-news warm-up is NOT re-applied -- the gate headline). FIEGARCH is the EGF MA(inf) convolution of observed g (future g=0, no recursion); the variance-recursion family is the ARCH(inf) iterate reusing the §33 kappa=E[(|eta|-gamma eta)^delta] for future news. sigma=(m_h)^(1/delta) [FIEGARCH: exp(lnsigma^2/2)] is the Jensen-biased plug-in, reproduced-not-corrected. FIEGARCH drops std/sstd (finding-3 continuous-df EGF gap); the 4 variance-recursion models fit all 8 laws (38 model,law triples). smooth_gsmooth.note: Phase-7 sub-build 1 (semiparametric, local-polynomial regression at a FIXED bandwidth). smoots::gsmooth(y, v=0, p, mu, b=0.15, bb) OUTPUT (clean-room: build from Feng-Gries-Fritz 2020 + Beran-Feng 2002, validate against gsmooth OUTPUT, never its Rcpp source). Input is the log-squared demeaned returns w_t = log((y_t - mean(y))^2) of synthetic_returns.csv (the semiparametric scale). gsmooth returns list(ye=fitted trend m_hat, orig, ws=[751x751] boundary weight matrix, res, v,p,mu,b,bb,n); fixtures store ye. Grid pins the conventions: p in {1,3} (locpol_spec poly orders; p-v must be odd, v=0), mu in {0,1,2,3} = {uniform, Epanechnikov, bisquare, triweight} second-order kernels K(x) proportional to (1-x^2)^mu on [-1,1], bb in {0,1} boundary = {fixed-bandwidth-one-side, k-nearest-neighbour} (smoots' bb; the fEGarch locpol_spec boundary_method extend/shorten correspondence is a sub-build-3 wiring item). Local weighted-LS: at each rescaled x_t in [0,1] fit a degree-p polynomial by WLS with kernel weights over |x_i-x_t|<=b, take the intercept (v=0) as m_hat(x_t). Bandwidth window 2*floor(n*b)+1 = 751. The clean-room build reproduces ye per (p,mu,bb).

smooth_ipi.note: Phase-7 sub-build 2 (IPI data-driven bandwidth selector, calls local_poly repeatedly to minimize AMISE). Input w_t = log((y_t-mean(y))^2) of synthetic_returns.csv (same as sub-build 1). Clean-room: build from Feng-Gries-Fritz 2020 + Beran-Feng 2002 + the esemifar paper (literature/), validate against smoots/esemifar OUTPUT, never their Rcpp source. TWO variants sharing the local_poly core but differing in the variance factor c_f and the bandwidth exponent: SHORT-memory (smoots::msmooth/tsmooth) and LONG-memory (esemifar::tsmoothlm). AMISE (Feng-Gries-Fritz): I[m^(k)] = int_{cb}^{db} {m^(k)}^2 dx (k=p+1), C1 = I[m^(k)]*beta_{nu,k}^2/(k!)^2, C2 = 2*pi*(db-cb)*R(K)*c_f/(n*h^{2nu+1}), AMISE(h)=h^{2(k-nu)}*C1 + C2; b_opt minimizes it (nu=0 => exponent 1/(2k+1) => 1/5 for p=1, 1/9 for p=3). Each iteration re-estimates c_f and I[m^(k)] at an INFLATED pilot bandwidth h_d = h^a; iterate to convergence or 40 iters. Inflation rate InfR: SHORT-memory Opt a = 5/7 (p=1) / 9/11 (p=3), Nai 5/9 / 9/13, Var 1/2; LONG-memory Opt a = (5-2d)/(7-2d) / (9-2d)/(11-2d), Nai (5-2d)/(9-2d) / (9-2d)/(13-2d), Var 1/2 -- i.e. the SM formulas are the LM formulas at d=0. c_f: SHORT-memory via Mcf (NP=Bartlett-window long-run variance / ARMA / AR / MA); LONG-memory via a FARIMA(p,d,q) fit to the detrended residuals (BIC over pmin..pmax, qmin..qmax; default (0,d,0)) whose fractional d enters both c_f and the inflation rate. cb=0.05 boundary cutoff (cb=0.05, db=0.95); bb boundary as in gsmooth; bStart=0.15. Returns: b0 (selected bandwidth), cf0 (variance factor), I2 (=I[m^(k)]), iterations (the bandwidth sequence across IPI steps -- validate the ITERATION, not just b0), niterations, ye (fitted trend at b0), plus (LM) d.BIC/p.BIC/q.BIC (the FARIMA error orders). DEFAULT RESULTS: SM b0=0.13278926 (6 iters), cf0=7.4266, I2=971.34, L0_opt=6; LM b0=0.14024950 (8 iters), cf0=0.81997, I2=1286.49, d.BIC=0.089891 (FARIMA(0,d,0)). meta JSONs also carry tuning-variant b0/iterations (SM: p3/InfR_Nai/Mcf_ARMA/mu3; LM: p3/InfR_Nai/farima11) to pin each param's effect. The clean-room build reproduces b0, the iteration sequence, cf0, I2, d (LM), and ye.

smooth_ipi_components.note: Phase-7 sub-build 2 ISOLATION fixtures -- pin the c_f estimators and the derivative-smoother SEPARATELY so the IPI iteration can be debugged piece by piece. All PINNED MACHINE-EXACT against smoots/esemifar OUTPUT (clean-room, papers only). (1) SM c_f (Mcf=NP): cf0 = g0 + 2*sum_{j=1}^{L}(1-j/(L+1))*gj -- the Bartlett long-run variance with BIASED autocovariances gj of the detrended residuals (res, at bvc='N' so res<->cf0 are consistent), L=L0.opt; reconstructed cf0=6.26053647 == fixture (1e-16). L0.opt is a DATA-DRIVEN lag (Buhlmann/Feng iterative-plug-in lag-window; observed L0.opt=3 at bvc='N', 6 at bvc='Y') -- the ONE sub-rule still to pin in the build (the fixture stores L0.opt so the Bartlett formula validates given L, and the lag rule validates separately). Alternative backends Mcf=ARMA/AR/MA fit a parametric model to res and use its long-run variance sigma^2*|theta(1)/phi(1)|^2 (cf0 recorded for reference). (2) LM c_f: cf0 = mean(FARIMA_innovations^2)/(2*pi) -- the EMPIRICAL innovation variance of the BIC-fit FARIMA(p,d,q) (NOT fracdiff's MLE sigma^2, which differs ~0.08%), times |theta(1)/phi(1)|^2 (=1 for (0,d,0)); reconstructed 0.81996780 == fixture (1e-16). The fractional d enters the inflation rate, NOT c_f. (3) Derivative smoother: gsmooth(v=k) = the sub-build-1 local_poly returning beta[v]*v!*n^v (the v-th derivative w.r.t. rescaled x=t/n; k=p_trend+1, derivative poly order p with p-v odd -- v2/p3 for trend p=1, v4/p5 for trend p=3); reconstructed to ~1e-9 (n^v amplifies the ~1e-15 relative FP error of the k-th derivative). I[m^(k)] = trapezoidal integral of {m^(k)}^2 over the [cb,db]=[0.05,0.95] interior grid (integration rule to confirm against I2 in the build).

semiparam_egarch_fixedbw.note: Phase-7 sub-build 3 (end-to-end semiparametric) RECON FIXTURE. fEGarch(egarch_spec(1,1), y, use_nonpar=TRUE, nonparspec=locpol_spec(bwidth=0.15)) -- a FIXED bandwidth. Model: r_t = mu + s(x_t)*lambda_t*eta_t; scale s via local-poly on y_t=ln((r_t-mu)^2) (m(x_t)=ln[s^2]+C_mu, C_mu=E[ln zeta^2]), then a ZERO-MEAN egarch on zeta_hat=r*/s_hat; sigt = s_hat*lambda_hat (total vol). RECON ANSWERS: (a) selector routing is by MODEL spec -- short-memory EGF (egarch) -> smoots (SM, needs Buhlmann L0.opt); long-memory EGF (fiegarch) -> esemifar (LM). (b) locpol_spec(bwidth=<0..0.5>) supplies a FIXED bandwidth and the auto IPI selector does NOT run (b0/niterations empty) -> fully deterministic, NO Buhlmann/FARIMA selector needed. (c) the validation target is fEGarch's semiparametric OUTPUT (scale_fun = s_hat, sigt = total vol, and the zero-mean egarch pars {omega_sig,phi1,kappa,gamma}), NOT smoots' internal bandwidth. CONSEQUENCE: with a FIXED bwidth the end-to-end fit is clean-room-reproducible -- scale machine-exact (local_poly + the C_mu=mean_log_sq retransform), egarch at the established fit tolerance (~1e-6) -- bypassing the blocked auto-selectors. The auto-bandwidth path (default bwidth=NULL) inherits the SM Buhlmann L0.opt blocker (egarch) or the LM FARIMA fit-tolerance (fiegarch). Fixture is at bwidth=0.15 (auto would select b0~0.1006 for egarch).

semiparam_fixedbw_fit.note: Phase-7 sub-build 3 BUILD-TARGET fixture: the end-to-end fEGarch semiparametric fit at a FIXED bandwidth (locpol_spec(poly_order=1, kernel_order=1, bwidth=0.15), n_test=0). The 6-step WP171 2.2.1 procedure, reconstructed MACHINE-EXACT for the scale: (1) ybar=mean(y); wtil_t=ln((y-ybar)^2); (2) mhat(x_t)=local_poly(wtil, v=0, p=1, mu=1, b=0.15, boundary=extend) [= nonpar_model$ye]; (3) C_T = -ln[ n^-1 * sum exp(uhat_t) ], uhat_t=wtil_t - mhat_t [the bias/retransform correction; C_T=-1.37547 here]; (4) shat(x_t)=exp((mhat - C_T)/2) -- reconstructs scale_fun with max|dev|=0 (exp((mhat-C_T)/2) == fEGarch scale_fun EXACTLY); (5) rhat=(y-ybar)/shat (= zeta_hat, the de-scaled returns); (6) a ZERO-MEAN EGF fit on rhat (EGARCH: {omega_sig,phi1,kappa,gamma}; FIEGARCH adds fractional d) -> lambda_hat (= sigtilde, parametric cond. sd of rhat), and the total volatility Omega_hat = sigt = shat * lambda_hat (lambda_hat mean ~0.97). KEY REFINEMENT vs the recon: at a FIXED bwidth BOTH egarch and fiegarch use the smoots scale machinery (nonpar_model class 'smoots') and the scale step is IDENTICAL + machine-exact (same C_T) -- the SM/LM selector routing only matters for AUTO bandwidth, which is bypassed. So steps 1-5 (scale) are machine-exact (reuse the sub-build-1 local_poly + the C_T correction); step 6 is the established EGF fit-tolerance (~1e-6). Decoupling confirmed: a standalone EGARCH on rhat matches the semiparam pars to ~1e-4 (phi1/gamma), the small gaps being the zero-mean-vs-mean-included constraint. The clean-room build wires local_poly + C_T + the existing EGF fit via these 6 steps; fully reproducible without the blocked auto-selectors. mu_hat = ybar exactly. etat = rhat/lambda_hat (fully standardized innovation).
